To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a protocol to simulate the dynamic environment of OR-odorant interaction and that the protocol is applicable to other members of the GPCR family.
the computational modeling of OR-odorant interaction is an effective approach to understanding the mechanism of odorant detection by ORs and that our methodology can be applied to other GPCRs.

the simulation of the dynamic environment of an OR-odorant interaction can provide a more complete view of the interaction than can be obtained from static docking alone, and that the simulation of an OR-odour interaction can provide insight into how the odor ligand binds to the OR.

developing a protocol for the computational structural modeling and simulation of the olfactory receptor.
the molecular basis of olfaction.
developing a methodology for the computational structural analysis of olfactory receptors and their interactions with ligands.

our methodology provides a robust, reproducible, and efficient means for generating all-atom simulations of OR-odorant binding.
our methodology is a powerful tool for the computational structural biologist and the computational medicinal chemist.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a protocol for simulating the interactions that occur between an OR and a ligand.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of simulating OR-odorant interaction in a dynamic, membrane-bound environment using an all-atom, explicit solvent, molecular dynamics (MD) protocol.
we have demonstrated the utility of molecular dynamics simulations in the study of OR-odorant complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the simulation of dynamic protein-ligand interactions is an essential step in the development and validation of computational models of ORs.

the simulation of OR-odorant complexes can be performed using the same computational protocols that are routinely employed to study the dynamics and function of other membrane proteins, such as ion channels and transporters.
computational modeling of ORs can be used to generate novel hypotheses that can be tested experimentally.
